Troponin elevated at 0.9 (repeat value); initial troponin bump noted, with repeat troponin rise to 0.9. Cardiology concurs this represents non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI).

Assessment

Patient is a 70-year-old with anemia who presented with troponin elevation. Initial troponin bump was initially attributed to demand ischemia from anemia; however, repeat troponin rose to 0.9. Cardiology was consulted and agrees the clinical picture is consistent with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). Heparin anticoagulation has been initiated per protocol.

Plan

1. Initiate heparin per protocol for NSTEMI.
2. Continue cardiology consultation and management.
3. Monitor troponin trend and clinical response to anticoagulation.

Hemoglobin 7.1 (down from 9.0). Gastroenterology examination revealed melena.

Assessment

Patient is a 67-year-old with dark stools and a significant drop in hemoglobin from 9.0 to 7.1. Gastroenterology examination documented melena, confirming an upper gastrointestinal bleed. The clinical picture is consistent with an acute upper GI hemorrhage, likely related to iron supplementation as a contributing factor. The patient requires urgent intervention and close monitoring.

Plan

1. Initiate pantoprazole drip for upper gastrointestinal bleed.
2. Schedule esophagogastroduodenoscopy for tomorrow.
